name: The Hundred Markets
descriptionSeed: Everything the world makes, in one place, sold by the people who make it. Rootkin grown-wood beside Enginewright mechanism beside Umbral harbored-goods beside things from Reaches nobody at the next stall can pronounce. Prices here are the truest prices in existence because every seller is standing next to their competitor from the opposite pole. It is loud, it is enormous, and it is the only economy in the world that has actually seen itself whole.
encounterFlavor: Traders from all twenty-four; a broker who can price anything; something for sale that should not be for sale, from a Reach that should not be selling it.
questSeeds: Someone is buying up one specific thing across every market, quietly, and nobody has noticed but you
A stall is selling harbored goods and the Harborward did not authorize it
worldPosNote: ⛑ CCODE-471 — BETWEEN THE HUB AND THE COLISEUM, which is Erik's own sentence and is a GEOMETRIC constraint, not a vibe: "the hundred markets are between the hub and the coliseum." Taken literally — the midpoint of the Axis Gate (0.2°, 0°) and the Coliseum (0.42°, 40°) carried back into polar coordinates, which is (0.29°, 27°). Gate→markets→coliseum measures 0.296 radii against 0.296 for gate→coliseum direct, so the three are collinear to one part in ten thousand and §346 gates it. Its old longitude of 200° put the trade ring on the OPPOSITE side of the world's axis from the arena it feeds. (SNG-180: authored position — WHERE it sits. Independent of axisVector, which is WHAT it is; a bastion is where the two disagree.)
appearance: A sprawling market of hundreds of stalls under mismatched canopies, packed along lanes too narrow for carts. Goods of every kind stacked shoulder-high — grown wood, machinery, cloth, sealed crates. Noise, awnings, and no clear edges.
